findings.title: time.Time compared with !=
findings.message: Comparing DateRange structs with != compares time.Time internals (wall, ext, loc pointer); equal civil dates with differing representations reset the draft anchor.
findings.suggestion: Compare civil keys and location instead of struct equality.

findings.title: Struct equality on time.Time values
findings.message: Calendar click handlers set p.anchor and return without any View refresh signal; more importantly, the closures capture stale state. After a Change, the caller updates p.Value but View's reset of anchor depends on p.accepted != p.Value comparing time.Time structs with ==, which compares Location pointers and monotonic data; semantically equal times can compare unequal, clearing the draft anchor unexpectedly on re-render.
findings.suggestion: Compare ranges via civilKey of Start and End plus location, not struct equality (p.accepted != p.Value).
findings.evidence: live := func() bool { return p.ID == id && !p.Disabled && p.Change != nil && p.Value.Start.Location() == loc }

findings.title: Unchecked ID slicing may panic
findings.message: Slicing n.ID[len(n.ID)-10:] panics if a CalendarCell button has an ID shorter than 10 bytes. Also, a Button with CalendarCell may exist for non-day cells (e.g. nav) whose ID does not end in a date; those are skipped only via parse error, which is fragile.
findings.suggestion: Guard with len(n.ID) >= 10 before slicing, or derive the date from CalendarCell metadata rather than parsing the ID.
